chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Cap'n Warmack's society band at Willie's Lakeshore Garden
summary: Crawford recalls the Cleveland society band that held the club job during the 1929 strike.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: We left Lakeside, Ohio, in '29. We decided to go north. So we went around the lake to Cleveland naturally I think you have that on there, but -- and the big band in Cleveland that held the job at the place we were supposed to go, Willie's Lakeshore Garden, most fabulous place in Cleveland, nightclub-wise.
And you had a band that held forth there -- am I saying that right, fort or forth?

Forth there -- was a band, colored band by the name of Cap'n -- that's for captain -- but Cap'n Warmack. Had a drummer in there by the name of Gene. I can't recall his name. Nice personality. But the band was a society band. Cap'n Warmack's band.

He didn't do too much swinging. This is society. They held the job. They held forth at Willie's Lakeshore Garden when that surprising musician's strike, waiter's strike was simultaneously done there. I don't know what they were thinking about because it was the height of the Depression, '29, and they decided to strike.
Oh, right, you told us -- you told me that on the earlier part of the tape, that that was why you all
didn't have any work for a long time.
